title: As He is, be (Mekhilta, Shirata 3)
hook: as God is gracious and merciful, so be gracious and merciful
tomorrow: how do you follow someone who is a fire?

segments.voice: Yesterday, at the sea: a servant girl saw more than the prophet Ezekiel. She saw more. Stay on that shore a minute, because the song she sang has one word a sage heard twice.

Everybody copies someone. An older cousin's laugh, a coach's handshake, the way a favorite singer signs her name. Now back to the shore. The water has closed behind them. Moses and the people are singing, and in the middle of the song comes a line the old Jewish translation gives as "This is my God, and I will glorify Him." Much later, in the Mekhilta, a book of midrash on Exodus, the sages stop on that last word. Glorify God? With what? A person can't add one thing to God. So what is the line asking for?
screen: `EVERYBODY COPIES SOMEONE.` → `THE SONG ON THE FAR SHORE.` → `GLORIFY GOD? WITH WHAT?`

segments.voice: The Hebrew word is ve'anvehu, and the Mekhilta gives more than one answer. Rabbi Ishmael says: make your mitzvot beautiful before God. A lovely sukkah, a lovely prayer shawl. Then a sage named Abba Shaul hears something hiding inside the word. Say it slowly and it echoes ani ve-hu: I and He. So he reads the verse as a job description. Be like Him. As He is gracious and merciful, so you be gracious and merciful. Look at what he picks. Not the power that split the sea. Not the judging. Of everything the song just praised, the part a person is asked to copy is mercy, two words from the list God gives Moses about Himself later in Exodus. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: the rabbis turned a sound inside a word into a way of life, and the way of life is kindness. The Talmud brings Abba Shaul's reading again, in tractate Shabbat. And it quietly changes what imitating God means. Nobody becomes God. You copy the one thing a person actually can: going easy on someone who can't pay you back. Yesterday a servant girl saw God at the sea. Abba Shaul asks what you do once you've seen.
screen: `TWO READINGS OF ONE WORD.` · `ANI VE-HU: I AND HE.` · `COPY THE MERCY, NOT THE POWER.` · `GO EASY ON SOMEONE.` · then, large: `AS HE IS, BE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who will need some grace from you this week: a little brother, a coworker running late, someone about to get something wrong in front of you. Picture the moment it happens. Now choose, ahead of time, one gracious thing you'll say or do, small enough that you'll really do it, and keep that plan in front of you while the bell rings out.
screen: `ONE PERSON.` · `THE MOMENT.` · `ONE GRACIOUS THING, CHOSEN NOW.`

segments.voice: As He is: Abba Shaul's reading of one word in the song at the sea. As God is gracious and merciful, so be gracious and merciful.
Your line: as he is, be. Of everything at the sea, mercy is the part a person can copy.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching often names imitating God's kindness as a duty: Abba Shaul's reading in the Mekhilta, and again in the Talmud (Shabbat 133b), is taught as 'be like Him: as He is gracious and merciful, so be gracious and merciful.'

chat.says: musical auditions. a freshman froze mid-song and kids laughed. i'm just the reader. stay neutral, right?
options: Neutral on her singing, not on her. A kind word and a fresh start.
Yes. Being kind to her would be unfair to everyone else trying out.
Laugh along gently so it feels like a joke instead of a fail.
chat.meaning: As God is gracious and merciful, so be. Mercy to a person isn't the same as rigging the result.
